newsitem.title: INDIA: Becton Dickinson to set up plant in India.
newsitem.headline: Becton Dickinson to set up plant in India.

text.p: Becton Dickinson, the Fortune 500 U.S.-based health care company, said on Tuesday it would build a $30 million plant in the northern Indian state of Haryana to produce medical equipment.
Company chairman Clateo Castellini told reporters the highly automated plant, to be operational by mid-1998, would be located at Bawal, some 90 km (56 miles) from Delhi.
"The facility will manufacture disposable needles, syringes and catheters. The manufacturing techniques will be of international standard and the products will be exported," a company statement said.
The statement said Becton expected a turnover of 400 million rupees ($11.11 million) in its first year of operations in 1996/97 (Oct-Sept).
Castellini said the investment would be increased to $100 million over the next five years.

Becton Dickinson operates in more than 80 countries. Among the products it makes are drug delivery and infusion systems, diabetes care devices, surgical devices, and microbiology and blood collection products.
